summary: One splice rule places every member: a leading `**/` collapses to zero segments and literal leading segments are fixed placement, so the `.md` hardcode goes

edit.description: `splice_name` becomes the one name-through-a-glob rule: strip a leading `**/` to zero segments, then admit exactly one `*` confined to the final segment (the existing `*/<file>` starred-segment admission unchanged) and treat literal leading segments as fixed placement; `member_projection_path` loses its `glob.contains("**")` → `format!("{name}.md")` arm, so a `json-document`/`toml-document` kind at `**/sub/*.json` lands `sub/<name>.json` rather than `<name>.md`. `FlatGlobDepth`'s doc comment and message restate the narrowed rule (multi-star, or a `*` outside the final segment) instead of the retired 'single-segment or any-depth' one.

The forced twin of the same rule: `spliceName` gains the `**/` collapse and the literal-leading-segment admission, `projectionPath` loses its `glob.includes("**")` → `${name}.md` branch, and `nestedFilePath`'s pattern splice stops refusing a multi-segment template path. The seam comment already states 'the two must agree'.

`a_single_star_and_any_depth_glob_project_to_the_expected_paths` asserts the `**/CLAUDE.md` member lands `CLAUDE.md` (the fixed-path class) rather than `<name>.md`; new cases cover the inbox reproduction (a `**/sub/*.json` kind's members landing `sub/<name>.json`) and a flat `sub/*.json` glob placing instead of refusing `FlatGlobDepth`.

The frozen-agreement lane's target set and its doc comment name the any-depth branch that no longer exists; add a target whose glob carries a literal leading segment so both derivations are gated on the widened rule.

A host template path with a literal leading segment (`notes/*.md`) now composes under the host's unit instead of refusing `FlatGlobDepth` — the case whose own error text told the author to use a nesting kind.

tests.asserts: a `**`-glob kind projects its own format's path (`sub/<name>.json`), `**/CLAUDE.md` lands the fixed `CLAUDE.md`, and a literal leading segment places rather than refusing
the SDK's `projectionPath` and the engine's `member_projection_path` still agree over every unit shape, now including a literal-leading-segment glob
a host template path carrying a leading literal directory composes `<host unit>/notes/<name>.md`

acceptance: `cargo test` and `pnpm --dir sdk test` green, with the projection-path seam lane passing over the widened rule; every built-in kind's projection is byte-unchanged (`memory`'s `CLAUDE.md`, `agent`'s `<name>.md`), so `temper emit` over `.temper/` rewrites nothing.
